#!/usr/bin/env Rscript
# Infer cell-cell communication networks for the Gide melanoma ICB cohort with RaCInG
# and summarize the most common interaction patterns across patients.

suppressMessages(library(RaCInG))

data_dir    <- "/home/marcelo.hurtado/Documents/tme_analysis/b0f19b8438/work/data"
results_dir <- "/home/marcelo.hurtado/Documents/tme_analysis/b0f19b8438/work/results"
dir.create(results_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

set.seed(1)

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 1. Load expression matrix (genes x samples) and undo log2(TPM + 1)
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
log2tpm <- as.matrix(read.table(
  file.path(data_dir, "Gide_log2TPM.txt"),
  header = TRUE, row.names = 1, sep = "\t", check.names = FALSE
))
tpm <- 2^log2tpm - 1
tpm[tpm < 0] <- 0

cat(sprintf("Gide cohort: %d genes x %d samples\n", nrow(tpm), ncol(tpm)))

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 2. Build RaCInG input matrices (deconvolution, LR prior network, LR matrix)
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
input <- prepare_input_files(
  counts          = tpm,
  output_folder   = results_dir,
  file_name       = "Gide",
  deconv_method   = "Quantiseq",
  already_normalized = TRUE,
  expr_threshold  = 10
)
saveRDS(input, file.path(results_dir, "Gide_racing_input.rds"))
cat("Cell types:", paste(input$celltypes, collapse = ", "), "\n")

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 3. Kernel method: direct cell-cell communication per patient
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
kernel_res <- compute_racing_kernel(
  input_data         = input,
  communication_type = "D",
  norm               = TRUE,
  remove_direction   = TRUE
)
saveRDS(kernel_res, file.path(results_dir, "Gide_kernel_result.rds"))

features <- kernel_res$features
write.csv(features, file.path(results_dir, "Gide_interaction_features_raw.csv"))

cat(sprintf("Interaction features: %d patients x %d cell-type pairs\n", nrow(features), ncol(features)))

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 4. Most common interaction patterns across the cohort
##    "Common" = how often a cell-type pair is among each patient's
##    strongest communication routes (top-K raw direct-communication scores).
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
topK <- 5
top_pairs_per_patient <- apply(features, 1, function(row) {
  names(sort(row, decreasing = TRUE))[seq_len(min(topK, length(row)))]
})

pair_counts <- table(unlist(as.list(as.data.frame(top_pairs_per_patient, stringsAsFactors = FALSE))))
pair_counts <- sort(pair_counts, decreasing = TRUE)

n_patients <- nrow(features)
common_patterns <- data.frame(
  Pair               = names(pair_counts),
  N_Patients_Top5    = as.integer(pair_counts),
  Pct_Patients_Top5  = round(100 * as.integer(pair_counts) / n_patients, 1),
  Mean_Raw_Score     = sapply(names(pair_counts), function(p) mean(features[, p])),
  Median_Raw_Score   = sapply(names(pair_counts), function(p) median(features[, p])),
  row.names = NULL
)
write.csv(common_patterns, file.path(results_dir, "Gide_most_common_interaction_patterns.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

cat("\nTop 10 most common cell-cell interaction patterns (by presence in each patient's top-5):\n")
print(head(common_patterns, 10))

## Secondary ranking: mean raw communication strength across the whole cohort
mean_ranked <- data.frame(
  Pair           = colnames(features),
  Mean_Raw_Score = colMeans(features),
  row.names = NULL
)
mean_ranked <- mean_ranked[order(-mean_ranked$Mean_Raw_Score), ]
write.csv(mean_ranked, file.path(results_dir, "Gide_interactions_ranked_by_mean_strength.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 5. Plot: frequency of the top common interaction patterns
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
top_n_plot <- min(15, nrow(common_patterns))
plot_df <- common_patterns[seq_len(top_n_plot), ]
plot_df$Pair <- factor(plot_df$Pair, levels = rev(plot_df$Pair))

png(file.path(results_dir, "Gide_most_common_interaction_patterns.png"), width = 1400, height = 900, res = 150)
par(mar = c(5, 14, 4, 2))
barplot(
  plot_df$Pct_Patients_Top5, names.arg = plot_df$Pair, horiz = TRUE, las = 1,
  col = "steelblue", xlab = "% of patients with this pair in their top-5 communication routes",
  main = sprintf("Most common cell-cell interaction patterns (Gide cohort, n = %d)", n_patients)
)
dev.off()

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 6. Ligand-receptor decomposition of the single most common pattern
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
top_pair <- as.character(common_patterns$Pair[1])
pair_celltypes <- strsplit(top_pair, "_")[[1]][-1]
sender   <- pair_celltypes[1]
receiver <- pair_celltypes[2]

lr_contrib <- computeLRContributions(
  Lmatrix = input$Lmatrix, Rmatrix = input$Rmatrix,
  Cmatrix = input$Cmatrix, LRmatrix = input$LRmatrix,
  celltypes = input$celltypes, sender = sender, receiver = receiver,
  patient_names = rownames(features)
)
write.csv(lr_contrib, file.path(results_dir, sprintf("Gide_LR_contributions_%s.csv", top_pair)), row.names = FALSE)

lr_plot <- plotLRContributions(lr_contrib, top_n = 10)
ggplot2::ggsave(file.path(results_dir, sprintf("Gide_LR_contributions_%s.png", top_pair)), lr_plot, width = 9, height = 6, dpi = 150)

cat(sprintf("\nMost common interaction pattern overall: %s (%s)\n", top_pair, pair_celltypes))
cat("Top ligand-receptor pairs driving it:\n")
print(head(lr_contrib, 10))

cat("\nDone. All results saved under:", results_dir, "\n")

#!/usr/bin/env Rscript
# Infer cell-cell communication networks for the Gide melanoma ICB cohort with RaCInG
# and summarize the most common interaction patterns across patients.

suppressMessages(library(RaCInG))

data_dir    <- "/home/marcelo.hurtado/Documents/tme_analysis/b0f19b8438/work/data"
results_dir <- "/home/marcelo.hurtado/Documents/tme_analysis/b0f19b8438/work/results"
dir.create(results_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

set.seed(1)

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 1. Load expression matrix (genes x samples) and undo log2(TPM + 1)
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
log2tpm <- as.matrix(read.table(
  file.path(data_dir, "Gide_log2TPM.txt"),
  header = TRUE, row.names = 1, sep = "\t", check.names = FALSE
))
tpm <- 2^log2tpm - 1
tpm[tpm < 0] <- 0

cat(sprintf("Gide cohort: %d genes x %d samples\n", nrow(tpm), ncol(tpm)))

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 2. Build RaCInG input matrices (deconvolution, LR prior network, LR matrix)
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
input <- prepare_input_files(
  counts          = tpm,
  output_folder   = results_dir,
  file_name       = "Gide",
  deconv_method   = "Quantiseq",
  already_normalized = TRUE,
  expr_threshold  = 10
)
saveRDS(input, file.path(results_dir, "Gide_racing_input.rds"))
cat("Cell types:", paste(input$celltypes, collapse = ", "), "\n")

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 3. Kernel method: direct cell-cell communication per patient
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
kernel_res <- compute_racing_kernel(
  input_data         = input,
  communication_type = "D",
  norm               = TRUE,
  remove_direction   = TRUE
)
saveRDS(kernel_res, file.path(results_dir, "Gide_kernel_result.rds"))

features <- kernel_res$features
write.csv(features, file.path(results_dir, "Gide_interaction_features_raw.csv"))

cat(sprintf("Interaction features: %d patients x %d cell-type pairs\n", nrow(features), ncol(features)))

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 4. Most common interaction patterns across the cohort
##    "Common" = how often a cell-type pair is among each patient's
##    strongest communication routes (top-K raw direct-communication scores).
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
topK <- 5
top_pairs_per_patient <- apply(features, 1, function(row) {
  names(sort(row, decreasing = TRUE))[seq_len(min(topK, length(row)))]
})

pair_counts <- table(unlist(as.list(as.data.frame(top_pairs_per_patient, stringsAsFactors = FALSE))))
pair_counts <- sort(pair_counts, decreasing = TRUE)

n_patients <- nrow(features)
common_patterns <- data.frame(
  Pair               = names(pair_counts),
  N_Patients_Top5    = as.integer(pair_counts),
  Pct_Patients_Top5  = round(100 * as.integer(pair_counts) / n_patients, 1),
  Mean_Raw_Score     = sapply(names(pair_counts), function(p) mean(features[, p])),
  Median_Raw_Score   = sapply(names(pair_counts), function(p) median(features[, p])),
  row.names = NULL
)
write.csv(common_patterns, file.path(results_dir, "Gide_most_common_interaction_patterns.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

cat("\nTop 10 most common cell-cell interaction patterns (by presence in each patient's top-5):\n")
print(head(common_patterns, 10))

## Secondary ranking: mean raw communication strength across the whole cohort
mean_ranked <- data.frame(
  Pair           = colnames(features),
  Mean_Raw_Score = colMeans(features),
  row.names = NULL
)
mean_ranked <- mean_ranked[order(-mean_ranked$Mean_Raw_Score), ]
write.csv(mean_ranked, file.path(results_dir, "Gide_interactions_ranked_by_mean_strength.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 5. Plot: frequency of the top common interaction patterns
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
top_n_plot <- min(15, nrow(common_patterns))
plot_df <- common_patterns[seq_len(top_n_plot), ]
plot_df$Pair <- factor(plot_df$Pair, levels = rev(plot_df$Pair))

png(file.path(results_dir, "Gide_most_common_interaction_patterns.png"), width = 1400, height = 900, res = 150)
par(mar = c(5, 14, 4, 2))
barplot(
  plot_df$Pct_Patients_Top5, names.arg = plot_df$Pair, horiz = TRUE, las = 1,
  col = "steelblue", xlab = "% of patients with this pair in their top-5 communication routes",
  main = sprintf("Most common cell-cell interaction patterns (Gide cohort, n = %d)", n_patients)
)
dev.off()

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 6. Ligand-receptor decomposition of the single most common pattern
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
top_pair <- as.character(common_patterns$Pair[1])
pair_celltypes <- strsplit(top_pair, "_")[[1]][-1]
sender   <- pair_celltypes[1]
receiver <- pair_celltypes[2]

lr_contrib <- computeLRContributions(
  Lmatrix = input$Lmatrix, Rmatrix = input$Rmatrix,
  Cmatrix = input$Cmatrix, LRmatrix = input$LRmatrix,
  celltypes = input$celltypes, sender = sender, receiver = receiver,
  patient_names = rownames(features)
)
write.csv(lr_contrib, file.path(results_dir, sprintf("Gide_LR_contributions_%s.csv", top_pair)), row.names = FALSE)

lr_plot <- plotLRContributions(lr_contrib, top_n = 10)
ggplot2::ggsave(file.path(results_dir, sprintf("Gide_LR_contributions_%s.png", top_pair)), lr_plot, width = 9, height = 6, dpi = 150)

cat(sprintf("\nMost common interaction pattern overall: %s (%s)\n", top_pair, pair_celltypes))
cat("Top ligand-receptor pairs driving it:\n")
print(head(lr_contrib, 10))

cat("\nDone. All results saved under:", results_dir, "\n")

#!/usr/bin/env Rscript
# Infer cell-cell communication networks for the Gide melanoma ICB cohort with RaCInG
# and summarize the most common interaction patterns across patients.

suppressMessages(library(RaCInG))

data_dir    <- "/home/marcelo.hurtado/Documents/tme_analysis/b0f19b8438/work/data"
results_dir <- "/home/marcelo.hurtado/Documents/tme_analysis/b0f19b8438/work/results"
dir.create(results_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

set.seed(1)

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 1. Load expression matrix (genes x samples) and undo log2(TPM + 1)
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
log2tpm <- as.matrix(read.table(
  file.path(data_dir, "Gide_log2TPM.txt"),
  header = TRUE, row.names = 1, sep = "\t", check.names = FALSE
))
tpm <- 2^log2tpm - 1
tpm[tpm < 0] <- 0

cat(sprintf("Gide cohort: %d genes x %d samples\n", nrow(tpm), ncol(tpm)))

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 2. Build RaCInG input matrices (deconvolution, LR prior network, LR matrix)
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
input <- prepare_input_files(
  counts          = tpm,
  output_folder   = results_dir,
  file_name       = "Gide",
  deconv_method   = "Quantiseq",
  already_normalized = TRUE,
  expr_threshold  = 10
)
saveRDS(input, file.path(results_dir, "Gide_racing_input.rds"))
cat("Cell types:", paste(input$celltypes, collapse = ", "), "\n")

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 3. Kernel method: direct cell-cell communication per patient
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
kernel_res <- compute_racing_kernel(
  input_data         = input,
  communication_type = "D",
  norm               = TRUE,
  remove_direction   = TRUE
)
saveRDS(kernel_res, file.path(results_dir, "Gide_kernel_result.rds"))

features <- kernel_res$features
write.csv(features, file.path(results_dir, "Gide_interaction_features_raw.csv"))

cat(sprintf("Interaction features: %d patients x %d cell-type pairs\n", nrow(features), ncol(features)))

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 4. Most common interaction patterns across the cohort
##    "Common" = how often a cell-type pair is among each patient's
##    strongest communication routes (top-K raw direct-communication scores).
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
topK <- 5
top_pairs_per_patient <- apply(features, 1, function(row) {
  names(sort(row, decreasing = TRUE))[seq_len(min(topK, length(row)))]
})

pair_counts <- table(unlist(as.list(as.data.frame(top_pairs_per_patient, stringsAsFactors = FALSE))))
pair_counts <- sort(pair_counts, decreasing = TRUE)

n_patients <- nrow(features)
common_patterns <- data.frame(
  Pair               = names(pair_counts),
  N_Patients_Top5    = as.integer(pair_counts),
  Pct_Patients_Top5  = round(100 * as.integer(pair_counts) / n_patients, 1),
  Mean_Raw_Score     = sapply(names(pair_counts), function(p) mean(features[, p])),
  Median_Raw_Score   = sapply(names(pair_counts), function(p) median(features[, p])),
  row.names = NULL
)
write.csv(common_patterns, file.path(results_dir, "Gide_most_common_interaction_patterns.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

cat("\nTop 10 most common cell-cell interaction patterns (by presence in each patient's top-5):\n")
print(head(common_patterns, 10))

## Secondary ranking: mean raw communication strength across the whole cohort
mean_ranked <- data.frame(
  Pair           = colnames(features),
  Mean_Raw_Score = colMeans(features),
  row.names = NULL
)
mean_ranked <- mean_ranked[order(-mean_ranked$Mean_Raw_Score), ]
write.csv(mean_ranked, file.path(results_dir, "Gide_interactions_ranked_by_mean_strength.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 5. Plot: frequency of the top common interaction patterns
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
top_n_plot <- min(15, nrow(common_patterns))
plot_df <- common_patterns[seq_len(top_n_plot), ]
plot_df$Pair <- factor(plot_df$Pair, levels = rev(plot_df$Pair))

png(file.path(results_dir, "Gide_most_common_interaction_patterns.png"), width = 1400, height = 900, res = 150)
par(mar = c(5, 14, 4, 2))
barplot(
  plot_df$Pct_Patients_Top5, names.arg = plot_df$Pair, horiz = TRUE, las = 1,
  col = "steelblue", xlab = "% of patients with this pair in their top-5 communication routes",
  main = sprintf("Most common cell-cell interaction patterns (Gide cohort, n = %d)", n_patients)
)
dev.off()

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 6. Ligand-receptor decomposition of the single most common pattern
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## Cell-type names can themselves contain "_", so split "Dir_<A>_<B>" by
## matching known celltypes rather than naively splitting on "_".
parse_pair <- function(pair_name, celltypes) {
  body <- sub("^Dir_", "", pair_name)
  for (ct in celltypes) {
    if (startsWith(body, paste0(ct, "_"))) {
      other <- substring(body, nchar(ct) + 2)
      if (other %in% celltypes) return(c(ct, other))
    }
  }
  stop("Could not parse cell types from pair name: ", pair_name)
}

top_pair <- as.character(common_patterns$Pair[1])
pair_celltypes <- parse_pair(top_pair, input$celltypes)
sender   <- pair_celltypes[1]
receiver <- pair_celltypes[2]

lr_contrib <- computeLRContributions(
  Lmatrix = input$Lmatrix, Rmatrix = input$Rmatrix,
  Cmatrix = input$Cmatrix, LRmatrix = input$LRmatrix,
  celltypes = input$celltypes, sender = sender, receiver = receiver,
  patient_names = rownames(features)
)
write.csv(lr_contrib, file.path(results_dir, sprintf("Gide_LR_contributions_%s.csv", top_pair)), row.names = FALSE)

lr_plot <- plotLRContributions(lr_contrib, top_n = 10)
ggplot2::ggsave(file.path(results_dir, sprintf("Gide_LR_contributions_%s.png", top_pair)), lr_plot, width = 9, height = 6, dpi = 150)

cat(sprintf("\nMost common interaction pattern overall: %s (%s)\n", top_pair, pair_celltypes))
cat("Top ligand-receptor pairs driving it:\n")
print(head(lr_contrib, 10))

cat("\nDone. All results saved under:", results_dir, "\n")

description: Where the RaCInG R package source and installed library live on this machine
metadata:
  type: reference
---

RaCInG (Random Cell-cell Interaction Generator) is an R package for inferring patient-specific cell-cell communication networks from bulk RNA-seq (kernel and Monte Carlo methods). Relevant locations:

- Source/dev checkout: `~/Documents/RaCInG_package` (R/, vignettes/RaCiNG.Rmd, README.md, man/ — full devtools-style package repo, not a git repo at the top level of the analysis workspace).
- Installed library: present under both `~/R/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu-library/4.3/RaCInG` and `.../4.4/RaCInG`.
- System R: `/opt/R/4.3.3/bin/Rscript` (this is the R that has RaCInG + its full dependency chain — multideconv, liana, OmnipathR, ADImpute, nnls, ggplot2 — installed).
- Cached ligand-receptor prior network (avoids a live OmniPath/liana network call): `~/.cache/R/RaCInG/curated_omni_network.rds`.
- Upstream Python implementation: github.com/SysBioOncology/RaCInG; paper: van Santvoort et al. 2025, Cell Reports Methods.
- There is also a conda env literally named `RaCInG` (`~/anaconda3/envs/RaCInG`), but it's a generic Spyder/data-science Python env with no RaCInG-specific package — the actual tool is the R package above, run via system R, not that conda env.

**How to apply:** For any RaCInG task, use `/opt/R/4.3.3/bin/Rscript` with `library(RaCInG)` rather than searching for a Python install or activating the `RaCInG` conda env. See [[feedback-racing-multideconv-quirks]] for gotchas when running the pipeline on real cohort data.

---
name: feedback-racing-multideconv-quirks
description: Known gotchas when running RaCInG::prepare_input_files() / compute_racing_kernel() on real cohort expression data
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

Two non-obvious issues hit when running the RaCInG R pipeline (see [[reference-racing-package-location]]) on real public cohort data (e.g. melanoma ICB cohorts distributed as `log2(TPM+1)` matrices):

1. **Sample names starting with a digit break `prepare_input_files()`.** `multideconv::compute.deconvolution()` internally sanitizes sample names with R's `data.frame`/`make.names()` rules (e.g. `"10_PD1_PRE"` -> `"X10_PD1_PRE"`), but `prepare_input_files()` then checks `rownames(deconv)` against the original `colnames(counts)` and errors with "Patient names in deconvolution estimates do not match those in the counts matrix." **Fix:** sanitize `colnames(counts)` yourself with `make.names(colnames(counts), unique = TRUE)` *before* calling `prepare_input_files()`/`compute_racing_kernel()`/`compute_racing_montecarlo()`, so both sides already agree. Keep a saved mapping (original -> sanitized) if the original IDs matter downstream.

2. **`multideconv::compute.deconvolution()` writes to a hardcoded relative `Results/` folder**, independent of the `output_folder` argument passed to `prepare_input_files()`. Don't be surprised to find a stray `Results/Deconvolution_<file_name>.csv` next to the working directory after a run — move/copy it into the intended output folder if you want everything consolidated in one place.

3. Public cohort files literally named `*_log2TPM.txt` in this workspace's `data/` folder are actually `log2(TPM + 1)`, not `log2(TPM)` (confirmed: zeros present, and the package's own `already_normalized` docs call out exactly this convention). Convert back with `2^x - 1` and clamp negatives to 0 before passing `already_normalized = TRUE`.

**How to apply:** Any time you (re-)run the RaCInG pipeline on a new cohort file in this workspace, apply the `2^x - 1` conversion and the `make.names()` sanitization up front, and check for a stray top-level `Results/` dir afterward.

description: Layout and contents of the b0f19b8438/work TME analysis workspace (melanoma ICB cohorts)
metadata:
  type: project
---

Working directory `~/Documents/tme_analysis/b0f19b8438/work` (not a git repo) holds tumor-microenvironment analyses using public melanoma immune-checkpoint-blockade (ICB) cohorts:

- `data/Gide_log2TPM.txt`, `data/Riaz_log2TPM.txt`: gene x sample `log2(TPM+1)` matrices (see [[feedback-racing-multideconv-quirks]] for the exact conversion needed).
- `data/colData_all.txt`: per-sample metadata (`rna_id`, `Sample_id`, `Timing`, `Response` [R/NR], `Therapy`, `Cohort`) spanning six published cohorts: Gide (73 samples), Hugo (26), Liu (107), MGH (40), Riaz (51), Van_allen (39).
- `results/`: output directory for analyses (RaCInG cell-cell communication results from the Gide cohort saved here as of 2026-10-30 — kernel-method features, most-common-interaction-pattern summary, LR contribution breakdown; built with `scripts/run_racing_gide.R` using `deconv_method = "Quantiseq"` for speed).
- `scripts/`: analysis scripts, e.g. `run_racing_gide.R`.

**How to apply:** When asked to analyze "the cohort" without specifying which, check `colData_all.txt` for the `Cohort` column to disambiguate; Response/Therapy/Timing columns are the natural grouping variables for RaCInG's `wilcox_group_test()` once features are computed.

content.text:
## Summary

I ran RaCInG (R package at `~/Documents/RaCInG_package`) on the Gide cohort (73 melanoma ICB patients, 18,979 genes) via its kernel method, using Quantiseq deconvolution into 10 immune/stromal cell types. Two fixes were needed along the way: converting the `log2(TPM+1)` matrix back to linear TPM, and pre-sanitizing sample names (multideconv silently renames digit-starting IDs internally, which otherwise breaks the pipeline).

**Most common interaction patterns** (defined as: how often a cell-type pair ranks in a patient's top-5 strongest direct-communication scores, across all 73 patients):

| Rank | Pair | % of patients |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | CD4 (non-reg) ↔ Neutrophils | 68.5% |
| 2 | CD4 (non-reg) ↔ Monocytes | 60.3% |
| 3 | Neutrophils ↔ Neutrophils (self) | 60.3% |
| 4 | Monocytes ↔ Neutrophils | 49.3% |
| 5 | CD4 (non-reg) ↔ CD4 (non-reg) (self) | 46.6% |

The top pattern (CD4⁺ T ↔ Neutrophil) is driven mainly by NRG3–ERBB2/ERBB3 and CD44/CSPG4–integrin signaling (see the LR dot plot).

All results — input matrices, kernel scores, the ranked pattern tables/plots, and the LR decomposition — are saved in `results/`. I also saved a few memory notes about the RaCInG package location and the multideconv quirks so future runs on this cohort (or Riaz) won't need to rediscover them.

content.text:
**1. Input data transformation**
Yes. `Gide_log2TPM.txt` is `log2(TPM+1)`, but RaCInG's `prepare_input_files()` needs linear-scale TPM when fed pre-normalized data. I converted with `TPM = 2^x - 1` and clamped any negative floating-point artifacts to 0, then called the function with `already_normalized = TRUE` (skipping RaCInG's internal `ADImpute::NormalizeTPM()`, which is for raw counts, not already-normalized TPM). Internally the package re-logs this back to `log2(TPM+1)` for the LR-matrix step, so no information was lost.

**2. Methods run / skipped**
Ran: `prepare_input_files()` (Quantiseq deconvolution, curated OmniPath/liana LR prior network from the local cache, NNLS expression profiles, default `fun_LR = min`) → `compute_racing_kernel()` with `communication_type = "D"` (direct communication only) → `computeLRContributions()` + `plotLRContributions()` on the single most common pair.

Skipped:
- Other deconvolution methods (CBSX, EpiDISH, DeconRNASeq, DWLS) — used Quantiseq only, for speed and because CBSX needs credentials I don't have.
- Monte Carlo method (`compute_racing_montecarlo()`) and GSCC — kernel method is deterministic and sufficient for direct communication scores; GSCC (connectivity) wasn't asked for.
- `wilcox_group_test()` / `correlate_features_with_score()` — no comparison group or continuous score was requested.
- LR-activity mode (MOON-based) — used default expression-based LR strength instead, no activity data provided.

**3. Non-default parameters**
- `deconv_method = "Quantiseq"` (default is all 5 methods) — speed/reliability, no CBSX credentials.
- `already_normalized = TRUE` (default FALSE) — required since input is pre-normalized TPM, not raw counts.
- `norm = TRUE` in `compute_racing_kernel()` (default FALSE) — requested so both raw and enrichment kernels were available; only the raw kernel was used in the final summary.
- `expr_threshold = 10` — left at default; not changed.

**4. Problems encountered**
- First run failed: `prepare_input_files()` errored with "Patient names in deconvolution estimates do not match those in the counts matrix." Root cause: `multideconv::compute.deconvolution()` internally sanitizes sample names via R's `make.names()` (e.g. `"10_PD1_PRE"` → `"X10_PD1_PRE"`), but the function then compares against the original, unsanitized `colnames(counts)`. Fix: pre-sanitized `colnames(tpm)` with `make.names(unique = TRUE)` before calling the pipeline, and saved an original↔sanitized ID mapping CSV.
- A stray `Results/` directory (capitalized, distinct from the intended `results/`) appeared containing `Deconvolution_<file_name>.csv` — `multideconv::compute.deconvolution()` writes there unconditionally, ignoring the `output_folder` argument. I moved the real-run file into `results/` and deleted the leftover debug artifact and empty directory (both cleanup steps outside `results/` required separate confirmation due to the destructive-op guard).

**5. Checks performed**
- Confirmed all 73 Gide columns match `colData_all.txt`'s `Cohort == "Gide"` rows (sample ID sanity check) before running.
- Confirmed no duplicate gene symbols in the input matrix.
- Checked the script's log for errors/warnings after both runs; only the expected `already_normalized` warning appeared.
- Verified output dimensions made sense (10 cell types, 55 non-trivial cell-type-pair features, 73 patients).
- Verified the pair-name parser against actual cell-type names (since Quantiseq cell-type names themselves contain underscores, which could break a naive string split) before trusting the sender/receiver extracted for the LR decomposition.
- Visually inspected both output plots to confirm they rendered as intended.

**6. Limits / caveats**
- "Most common pattern" is defined by my own choice (presence in each patient's top-5 raw direct-communication scores, `topK = 5`) — not a built-in RaCInG statistic; a different top-K or a mean/enrichment-based ranking could shift the ordering, especially among the mid-ranked pairs.
- Single-method (Quantiseq) deconvolution only; results may differ with other/combined deconvolution methods, which the package supports but I didn't run for speed.
- Kernel method only — no Monte Carlo uncertainty estimates (no mean/sd across simulated graphs), so there's no measure of per-patient stochastic variability in these scores.
- No clinical grouping (e.g. Response) was incorporated, so this describes the cohort's general communication landscape, not response-associated differences.
- LR decomposition was shown only for the single top pair; other high-ranking pairs weren't broken down into ligand-receptor detail.

If you did not produce an item, skip it and say so. If you produced several variants, export the one you presented as your main result. Tables are CSV files with one row per patient and a first column named `patient` holding the sample names exactly as in the input data, unless said otherwise.

- ligands.csv: the ligands assigned to each cell type (the cell type x ligand matrix of the prepared input, "Lmatrix"), one row per assignment, with columns cell_type and ligand (not one row per patient).
- receptors.csv: the receptors assigned to each cell type ("Rmatrix"), one row per assignment, with columns cell_type and receptor (not one row per patient).
- direct_interactions.csv: the direct-interaction features of the kernel method, not normalised and without direction: one column per unordered pair of cell types, named "<cell type A> - <cell type B>" with the cell-type names exactly as in ligands.csv. This is what RaCInG returns when the direction is removed; if you only have the features with direction, a column "A - B" is A->B plus B->A, and a column "A - A" is twice A->A.

Finish with a one-line list of the files written.

#!/usr/bin/env Rscript
# Convert already-produced RaCInG results (results/*.rds, results/*.csv) into
# standard-format CSVs under results/standard/. No new computation.

results_dir  <- "/home/marcelo.hurtado/Documents/tme_analysis/b0f19b8438/work/results"
out_dir      <- file.path(results_dir, "standard")
dir.create(out_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

input      <- readRDS(file.path(results_dir, "Gide_racing_input.rds"))
kernel_res <- readRDS(file.path(results_dir, "Gide_kernel_result.rds"))
id_map     <- read.csv(file.path(results_dir, "Gide_sample_id_mapping.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

celltypes <- input$celltypes

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## ligands.csv : Lmatrix (cell type x ligand) -> long format
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
Lmatrix <- input$Lmatrix
lig_idx <- which(Lmatrix == 1, arr.ind = TRUE)
ligands_df <- data.frame(
  cell_type = rownames(Lmatrix)[lig_idx[, "row"]],
  ligand    = colnames(Lmatrix)[lig_idx[, "col"]]
)
ligands_df <- ligands_df[order(ligands_df$cell_type, ligands_df$ligand), ]
write.csv(ligands_df, file.path(out_dir, "ligands.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## receptors.csv : Rmatrix (cell type x receptor) -> long format
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
Rmatrix <- input$Rmatrix
rec_idx <- which(Rmatrix == 1, arr.ind = TRUE)
receptors_df <- data.frame(
  cell_type = rownames(Rmatrix)[rec_idx[, "row"]],
  receptor  = colnames(Rmatrix)[rec_idx[, "col"]]
)
receptors_df <- receptors_df[order(receptors_df$cell_type, receptors_df$receptor), ]
write.csv(receptors_df, file.path(out_dir, "receptors.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## direct_interactions.csv : kernel features (raw, direction already removed)
## columns "Dir_<A>_<B>" -> "<A> - <B>"; rows renamed to original sample IDs
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
features <- kernel_res$features

parse_pair <- function(pair_name, celltypes) {
  body <- sub("^Dir_", "", pair_name)
  for (ct in celltypes) {
    if (startsWith(body, paste0(ct, "_"))) {
      other <- substring(body, nchar(ct) + 2)
      if (other %in% celltypes) return(c(ct, other))
    }
  }
  stop("Could not parse cell types from pair name: ", pair_name)
}

new_colnames <- vapply(colnames(features), function(cn) {
  pair <- parse_pair(cn, celltypes)
  paste(pair[1], "-", pair[2])
}, character(1))

direct_df <- as.data.frame(features)
colnames(direct_df) <- new_colnames

patient_ids <- id_map$Sample_id[match(rownames(features), id_map$RaCInG_id)]
if (anyNA(patient_ids)) stop("Could not map all RaCInG patient IDs back to original sample IDs.")

direct_df <- cbind(patient = patient_ids, direct_df)
write.csv(direct_df, file.path(out_dir, "direct_interactions.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

cat("Written:\n")
cat(" -", file.path(out_dir, "ligands.csv"), sprintf("(%d rows)\n", nrow(ligands_df)))
cat(" -", file.path(out_dir, "receptors.csv"), sprintf("(%d rows)\n", nrow(receptors_df)))
cat(" -", file.path(out_dir, "direct_interactions.csv"), sprintf("(%d patients x %d pairs)\n", nrow(direct_df), ncol(direct_df) - 1))

#!/usr/bin/env Rscript
# Convert already-produced RaCInG results (results/*.rds, results/*.csv) into
# standard-format CSVs under results/standard/. No new computation.

results_dir  <- "/home/marcelo.hurtado/Documents/tme_analysis/b0f19b8438/work/results"
out_dir      <- file.path(results_dir, "standard")
dir.create(out_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

input      <- readRDS(file.path(results_dir, "Gide_racing_input.rds"))
kernel_res <- readRDS(file.path(results_dir, "Gide_kernel_result.rds"))
id_map     <- read.csv(file.path(results_dir, "Gide_sample_id_mapping.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

celltypes <- input$celltypes

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## ligands.csv : Lmatrix (cell type x ligand) -> long format
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
Lmatrix <- input$Lmatrix
lig_idx <- which(Lmatrix == 1, arr.ind = TRUE)
ligands_df <- data.frame(
  cell_type = rownames(Lmatrix)[lig_idx[, "row"]],
  ligand    = colnames(Lmatrix)[lig_idx[, "col"]]
)
ligands_df <- ligands_df[order(ligands_df$cell_type, ligands_df$ligand), ]
write.csv(ligands_df, file.path(out_dir, "ligands.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## receptors.csv : Rmatrix (cell type x receptor) -> long format
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
Rmatrix <- input$Rmatrix
rec_idx <- which(Rmatrix == 1, arr.ind = TRUE)
receptors_df <- data.frame(
  cell_type = rownames(Rmatrix)[rec_idx[, "row"]],
  receptor  = colnames(Rmatrix)[rec_idx[, "col"]]
)
receptors_df <- receptors_df[order(receptors_df$cell_type, receptors_df$receptor), ]
write.csv(receptors_df, file.path(out_dir, "receptors.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## direct_interactions.csv : kernel features (raw, direction already removed)
## columns "Dir_<A>_<B>" -> "<A> - <B>"; rows renamed to original sample IDs
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
features <- kernel_res$features

parse_pair <- function(pair_name, celltypes) {
  body <- sub("^Dir_", "", pair_name)
  for (ct in celltypes) {
    if (startsWith(body, paste0(ct, "_"))) {
      other <- substring(body, nchar(ct) + 2)
      if (other %in% celltypes) return(c(ct, other))
    }
  }
  stop("Could not parse cell types from pair name: ", pair_name)
}

new_colnames <- vapply(colnames(features), function(cn) {
  pair <- parse_pair(cn, celltypes)
  paste(pair[1], "-", pair[2])
}, character(1))

direct_df <- as.data.frame(features)
colnames(direct_df) <- new_colnames

patient_ids <- id_map$Sample_id[match(rownames(features), id_map$RaCInG_id)]
if (anyNA(patient_ids)) stop("Could not map all RaCInG patient IDs back to original sample IDs.")

direct_df <- cbind(patient = patient_ids, direct_df)
write.csv(direct_df, file.path(out_dir, "direct_interactions.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

cat("Written:\n")
cat(" -", file.path(out_dir, "ligands.csv"), sprintf("(%d rows)\n", nrow(ligands_df)))
cat(" -", file.path(out_dir, "receptors.csv"), sprintf("(%d rows)\n", nrow(receptors_df)))
cat(" -", file.path(out_dir, "direct_interactions.csv"), sprintf("(%d patients x %d pairs)\n", nrow(direct_df), ncol(direct_df) - 1))

input <- readRDS("results/Gide_racing_input.rds")

cat("rownames(csv)[perm]:\n"); print(rownames(L_csv)[perm])
'

message:
One last step. Save copies of the results you already produced in a standard format, so that they can be compared with other analyses. Do not compute anything new, do not rerun any method and do not change any existing result: only convert what already exists. Put the files in results/standard/. If you did not produce an item, skip it and say so. If you produced several variants, export the one you presented as your main result. Tables are CSV files with one row per patient and a first column named `patient` holding the sample names exactly as in the input data, unless said otherwise.

- ligands.csv: the ligands assigned to each cell type (the cell type x ligand matrix of the prepared input, "Lmatrix"), one row per assignment, with columns cell_type and ligand (not one row per patient).
- receptors.csv: the receptors assigned to each cell type ("Rmatrix"), one row per assignment, with columns cell_type and receptor (not one row per patient).
- direct_interactions.csv: the direct-interaction features of the kernel method, not normalised and without direction: one column per unordered pair of cell types, named "<cell type A> - <cell type B>" with the cell-type names exactly as in ligands.csv. This is what RaCInG returns when the direction is removed; if you only have the features with direction, a column "A - B" is A->B plus B->A, and a column "A - A" is twice A->A.

Finish with a one-line list of the files written.
